title: Gain, ERP and antenna efficiency
blurb: Convert dBi and dBd, calculate ERP and EIRP, and explain what makes an antenna efficient.

E9A01.why: An isotropic radiator is hypothetical and lossless, radiating equally in **all directions**. That makes it a perfect zero point for measuring gain.
E9A01.trap: Real calibrated antennas always have some pattern; only the imaginary one is isotropic.

E9A02.trap: Skipping the losses gives 150 × 5 = 750 W; use every dB in the chain.

E9A03.why: **Effective radiated power** is transmitter power after every loss and gain, as radiated in the beam direction.
E9A03.trap: Apparent power and power factor belong to AC circuits, not antennas.

E9A04.why: Nearby ground interacts with the antenna, so **antenna height** changes the feed point impedance. Feed line length, tuner and power do not.
E9A04.trap: A tuner or line length changes what the transmitter sees, not the antenna's own feed point.

E9A05.why: Reflections off the ground add to the direct wave, raising signal strength in some directions. That is **ground gain**.

E9A07.why: dBi gain, so this is EIRP. Net = 7 − 2 − 2.8 − 1.2 = **+1 dB**, ratio 1.259. 200 W × 1.259 = **252 W**.

E9A08.why: Fresnel zone radius grows with wavelength. **5.8 GHz** has the shortest wavelength of the choices, so the smallest zone.
E9A08.trap: Lower frequency means longer wavelength and a fatter zone.

E9A09.why: Efficiency is the part of the total resistance that radiates: **radiation resistance ÷ total resistance**.
E9A09.trap: Total over radiation resistance would exceed 100%.

E9A10.why: Ground losses are a big loss resistance in a vertical. **Radials** lower it, so more of the power is radiated.
E9A10.trap: Shortening the element lowers radiation resistance, which makes efficiency worse.

E9A11.why: Current flowing through the soil heats it. How much it wastes depends on **soil conductivity**, which sets the ground loss resistance.

E9A12.why: A dipole is 2.15 dBi, so dBd = dBi − 2.15 = 6 − 2.15 = **3.85 dBd**.
E9A12.trap: Adding 2.15 gives 8.15, the wrong direction: dBd is the smaller number.
